description: TerraPulse combines NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS satellite data into one interactive global dashboard, making it easier to visualize, explore, and monitor active fire hotspots around the world.
summary:
TerraPulse is an interactive satellite fire monitoring platform that brings together active fire observations from NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS instruments in one unified interface.

Using data from NASA’s Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS), we developed a web-based dashboard that allows users to explore satellite-detected hotspots through an interactive geographic map, filter observations by sensor, and compare detection patterns.

One of TerraPulse’s key features is its sensor agreement and disagreement analysis, which highlights where observations from different satellite systems overlap and where they differ. This helps users investigate how different instruments observe fire activity and understand the variations between their datasets.

By making multiple sources of satellite fire information easier to explore and compare, TerraPulse aims to support a clearer understanding of Earth observation data and make comparative environmental monitoring more accessible.
details:
TerraPulse is an interactive satellite fire-monitoring platform that combines active fire observations from NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS instruments into one unified interface.

Using data from NASA’s Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS), we developed a web-based dashboard that allows users to explore satellite-detected hotspots on an interactive map, filter observations by sensor, and compare detection patterns.

A key feature of TerraPulse is its sensor agreement and disagreement analysis, which identifies areas where observations from different satellite systems overlap and where they differ. This allows users to investigate variations between datasets and better understand how different satellite instruments observe fire activity.

By bringing these observations together, TerraPulse makes satellite fire data more accessible and easier to interpret. It aims to support comparative environmental monitoring, encourage exploration of Earth observation data, and provide a foundation for further analysis of fire activity.
